messages:
Maya (CSM): Heads up - SentryBridge private deploy hit a KMS 403 this morning when trying to encrypt app data. Customer stressed about timeline, flagged renewal risk if unresolved in 10 days. Can @Ravi or @Ana triage?
Ravi (Infra): Do we have the exact AWS error and the role ARN? Also confirm if they use NAT egress or KMS VPC endpoints.
Maya (CSM): Error copy from customer: `ClientError: An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Encrypt operation: User is not authorized to perform kms:Encrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh`
Role: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/sentrybridge-app-Role
They said they route egress via managed NAT; no KMS endpoint today.
Ana (Security): Likely key policy or IAM condition with aws:SourceVpc/aws:SourceIp. If SNAT via NAT, SourceIp won't match. Can someone paste the key policy? If it uses SourceVpc we can add the VPC ID or explicitly allow the role ARN.
Ethan (Solutions): Fast remediation options: 1) Create KMS Interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) so SourceVpc matches. 2) Temporarily add the role ARN to key policy with tight actions and TTL. 3) Use dedicated NAT with static egress IPs and whitelist those IPs in key policy.
Maya (CSM): Customer said adding endpoints needs infra approval and subnet capacity; they'd prefer a quick policy tweak if possible.
Ana (Security): Okay short-term we can add a minimal policy statement to allow only kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt for that role, audit it, and roll back once endpoint exists. I'll draft snippet and rollback steps. Need CS signoff on customer approval.
Ravi (Infra): I'll validate if we can provision an Interface endpoint in their subnets. If not, proposal B: provision a small dedicated NAT with elastic IPs to keep SourceIp stable for key policy checks. Will report EOD.
Maya (CSM): Also customer noticed their Splunk forwarder strips some KMS requestParameters in proxies, which makes auditing harder. Any guidance?
Ethan (Solutions): Splunk forwarders sometimes truncate HTTP body. Ask them to enable full payload capture for the forwarder and test with a raw `aws kms encrypt` from a VM in the VPC. I'll send a checklist.
Ana (Security): Also request CloudTrail logs (KMS data events) for the timeframe - CloudTrail will show exact principal, keyId, and sourceIp. That's authoritative for policy tuning.
Maya (CSM): Action items: 1) Ravi: endpoint feasibility + subnet/SG plan or NAT alternative (owner: Ravi). 2) Ana: minimal key-policy snippet + audit/rollback plan (owner: Ana). 3) Ethan: Splunk forwarder checklist + test steps (owner: Ethan). 4) Maya: schedule 30m customer call Tue 09:00 PT to review and get signoff.
Ravi (Infra): Noted. If we add endpoint, reuse existing ENI SG patterns; will include security group and subnet IDs.
Ana (Security): Draft minimal policy (example): `{"Sid":"AllowSentryBridgeRoleTemp","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/sentrybridge-app-Role"},"Action":["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":"*"}` Include a Condition if customer insists on IP/VPC restrictions.
Ethan (Solutions): Splunk checklist: enable raw payload, increase sampling to 100% for test window, confirm UF version >=8.x, and capture a single raw CLI encrypt for comparison.
